key_insight: OpenSearch-VL provides a fully open, end-to-end recipe (data, trajectory synthesis, and training settings) that makes high-performing multimodal deep search agents reproducible and extensible for the community.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of open high-quality training data, transparent trajectory synthesis pipelines, and detailed training recipes that prevent reproducing state-of-the-art multimodal search agents.
method: Curate and release open multimodal training data tailored for deep search tasks (queries, web/evidence snapshots, and multimodal context).
Design a transparent trajectory synthesis pipeline that generates stepwise search/evidence-verification actions and supervision signals for agents.
Provide a complete training recipe (model architecture choices, loss functions, curriculum, and evaluation suite) to train and benchmark frontier vision-language search agents.
impact: Enables reproducible research and faster iteration on multimodal search agents, lowering barriers for labs and practitioners to develop, evaluate, and extend deep search capabilities in vision-language models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data → trajectory synthesis → training → agent inference (with callouts for open assets).
Example search trajectory: query → intermediate steps (retrieval, verification) → final answer, shown as a storyboard.
Dataset composition chart: proportions of image/text/evidence types and annotation sources.
Benchmark comparison bar chart: OpenSearch-VL vs prior closed or partial baselines on key metrics (accuracy, reasoning steps, reproducibility indicators).
paper_title: OpenSearch-VL: An Open Recipe for Frontier Multimodal Search Agents
paper_authors: Shuang Chen, Kaituo Feng, Hangting Chen, Wenxuan Huang, Dasen Dai
